BA.rationale: Boeing is in the early innings of a genuine operational turnaround — H1 2026 deliveries at 314 (best since 2018), revenue up 14% YoY, net losses narrowing sharply, and the balance sheet repaired from negative to positive equity. The FAA's restoration of self-certification authority on July 20, 2026 is a tangible vote of confidence. However, the stock is priced at 73x earnings and 27.5x book for a business generating -179M in quarterly operating cash flow with 2.5% net margins. The 1.4% earnings yield sits 330bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.71%, creating an unfavorable relative-value argument. The 47B debt load against only 6B equity leaves zero margin of safety. The DOJ's pursuit of criminal charges for breaching the 2021 DPA, 777X certification delays, and the CEO's own admission that Boeing needs 'a couple more years' to repair finances all underscore that the distance between current performance and normalized free-cash-flow generation is still significant. The valuation demands a rapid, sustained margin expansion that the available data cannot yet confirm. In a rising-rate environment, the risk-reward is asymmetric to the downside.
key_factors: Q1 2026 revenue of $22.22B represents +14.0% YoY gain over Q1 2025's $19.50B, signaling improved delivery cadence
Q1 2026 net income was -$7M (EPS -$0.11) versus Q1 2025's -$31M (EPS -$0.16) and Q2 2025's -$612M (EPS -$0.92) — loss compression is real
Net margin flipped from -14.2% (through April 2026) to +2.5% by May 2026 — a regime change in reported profitability
Q1 2026 operating cash flow was -$179M, a massive improvement over Q1 2025's -$1.62B but still negative
Total equity swung from -$3.30B (Q2 2025) to +$5.99B in Q1 2026 — a ~$9.3B improvement; total debt declined from $53.14B to $46.96B
Debt-to-equity stands at 7.84x — still extremely leveraged with $47B debt against only $6B equity
PE of 72.9x, P/B of 27.5x, earnings yield of 1.4% sits 330bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.71%
H1 2026 deliveries at 314 jets — strongest first half since 2028; Q2 included 129 737s and 25 787s
FAA restored Boeing's self-certification authority for 737 MAX and 787 starting July 20, 2026
777X certification risk resurfaces — reports of renewed FAA scrutiny could push entry-into-service into late 2020s
DOJ moving toward criminal charges after determining Boeing breached its 2021 Deferred Prosecution Agreement
CEO Kelly Ortberg stated Boeing needs 'a couple more years' to repair finances before launching a new aircraft program
10-year Treasury yield at 4.71% (+36 bps over lookback), 2-year at 4.37% (+59 bps) — rising rates amplify discount-rate penalty for highly leveraged company
Oil at $93.08/bbl — pressures airline profitability and could slow aircraft orders
Price has declined -9.5% from Q1 filing date ($231.28 on Apr 22) to $209.23, and -16.4% from Jan 21 level of $250.07
